full_judgment:
"Though the successors-in-interest of deceased Ilias Miah or not would be sorted out in the aforesaid Title Suit No. 245 of 1979 and Title Suit No. 344 of 1990 but for the purpose of these Miscellaneous Cases. I am of the view that the pre-emptors have, prima facie made out a case that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah or at least that they are the heirs of Ilias Miah in respect of the case land and thereby making them co-sharer tenants in the case land. Accordingly, on the basis of purchase from Kulsuma and Rahima by the pre-emptors, they also became the co-sharer tenants in the case land and as such the applications for pre-emption are maintainable at the instance of the pre-emptors as they had an interest in the case holding as co-sharer tenants." 

 8. The High Court Division has reversed the judgment and order of the court of appeal below upon observing that "the pre-emptors have, prima facie made out a case that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah or at least that they are the heirs of Ilias Miah in respect of the case land and thereby making them co-sharer tenants in the case land." 

 9. PW 1 in his evidence has stated that Ilias Miah died leaving wife Ful Banu, two sisters Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi and brother Yunus. But at the same time PW 1 has stated that he has not filed paper to show that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah and that he came to know from the papers which he had seen at the time of making purchase that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the full sisters of Ilias Miah and they are the daughters of Meherullah. It may be mentioned Ilias Miah is the son of Meherullah. Although PW 1 stated that he came to know from the papers which he saw at the time of making purchase but no such paper was placed before the court in support of his statement of knowing about Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi being the daughters of Meherullah. This witness has further stated that he heard from the relations of Rahim a Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi they are the full sisters of llias Miah but in support of having that information or deriving of the knowledge that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the full sisters of I1ias Miah, no evidence has been led. There is nothing in the evidence of PW 1 that he had any information from PW 2 who claims him to be the husband of Kulsuma Bibi, that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah. So PW 1's evidence as to that Rahima Bibi Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah remains uncorroborated or in other words has not been corroborated by the evidence of any of the witnesses examined by the pre-emptors. Now there remains the evidence of PW 2 who claims himself to be husband of Kulsuma Bibi. This witness has stated that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of I1ias Miah and he is the husband of Kulsuma Bibi. The fact of Rahirna Bibi's and Kulsuma Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah has been denied by the pre-emptees and thereupon it was the duty of the pre-emptors to establish the fact of Kulsuma's and Rahima's being the sisters of Ilias Miah because in the absence of establishing the said fact pre-emptors would not be entitled to have the relief prayed in Miscellaneous Cases. The pre-emptors to prove the fact that Rahima Bibi and Kulsuma Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah have examined PW 2. There is no tangible material except the uncorroborated statement of PW 2 that he is the husband of Kulsuma Bibi or in other words PW 2's claim as of being the husband of Kulsuma Bibi has not been corroborated by any other evidence, both oral and documentary. Because of the quality of the evidence of PW 2 it cannot be said that said witness has proved the pre-emptor's claim that Kulsuma and Rahima are the sisters of Ilias Miah. PW 2 claimed that his marriage was registered and that he has the Kabinama. But same has not been produced at any stage of the Miscellaneous Cases. In the background of challenge as to PW 2's being the husband of Kulsuma, said to be the daughter of Meherullah and thereupon full sister of Ilias Miah, the fact of PW 2's being husband of Kulsuma remains legally unestablished. The Kabinnama or any other competent person if would have deposed about the fact of Kulsuma's being wife of PW 2 that could have been the best evidence to resolve the contentious matter' that Kulsuma Bibi is the full sister of Ilias Miah and that PW 2 is the husband of Kulsuma Bibi but that vital material piece of evidence and the evidence of such person has not been brought on record. In the background of the evidence from the side of the pre-emptors as discussed herein above it is seen that the material question i.e. question of Rahima Bibi's and Kulsuma Bibi's being the full' sisters of I1ias Miah has not been resolved by legal evidence and that the evidence of PWs 1 and 2 having not been corroborated by the evidence of independent and reliable witness the same cannot be made the basis for coming to the decision that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah. Evidence of PWs 1 and 2 in no standard can be considered corroborative evidence of each other's evidence as to the material fact Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Miah or that PW 2 is husband of Kulsuma. The High Court Division in our view was in error in reversing the judgment of the court of appeal below upon observing; "pre-emptors have prima facie made a case that Rahima and Kulsuma are the sisters of Ilias Miah or at least that they are the heirs of Ilias Miah in respect of the case land and thereby making them co-sharer tenants in the case land" as pre-emptees in case of allowing pre-emption would be deprived of their valuable right to hold property in the absence of firm establishment of the fact that Kulsuma and Rahima are the sisters of Ilias Miah and as such the pre-emptors under the law are required to establish a definite and firm case and not a 'prima facie' case of their being co-sharers of the land sought to be pre-empted. Making out of prima case however strong be, in law cannot be the basis for depriving one of holding property and that to deprive one of one's property there must have case of definite and unassailable kind or quality. In pre- emption proceeding one is deprived of one's property through the coercive' process of the Court and as such unless pre-emptor has a positive case of his being co-sharer the court upon a finding of pre-emptor's having a 'prima facie case' of being co- sharer is not permitted by law to grant pre-emption. Right to acquire and to hold property, subject to restriction imposed by law, is a guaranteed right of a citizen and when a citizen by the coercive process of law is compelled to part with his acquired property, then the condition(s) or the provision of law upon resorting to which a citizen is compelled to part with his property, the same is to be fulfilled in entirety and the provision of law as to coercive parting with properly is to be applied only when there is proof of the fact up to the hilt in the background of which parting with property can be compelled or in other words a citizen would only be compelled to part with his acquired property while the other, who is seeking aid of the court to compel a citizen to part with his property, has established the fact that would have entitled him to have the other's property completely. One cannot compel another upon restoring to a particular provision of law to part with his property in making out a prima facie case for such parting with, as in the instant case of pre-emption. One has to establish one's basis of claim for compelling another to part with his property in one's favour to the full or finally but not upon making out a prima facie case for compelling one to part with one's property by the coercive process of law. In the instant case pre-emptors where required to establish that they are co- sharers of the land transferred to the pre-emptee of the respective Miscellaneous cases and for that pre-emptors were required to establish that Kulsuma and Rahima are the full sisters of Ilias Miah as because in the absence of establishing that Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Miah, since the pre-emptors claim they are co-sharers of the land transferred to pre-emptee of the two miscellaneous cases by purchase from sisters of Ilias Miah, the pre-emptors could not claim pre-emption in .respect of the transfers sought to be pre-empted. The appellate court dismissed the miscellaneous case on the finding that pre-emptors failed- to establish that Kulsuma and Rahima are full sisters of Ilias Mia. The High Court Division allowed the prayer for pre-emption on the finding that pre-emptors made out a prima facie case that Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Miah. The law is now settled that concept of "prima facie case" would only receive consideration of the court while disposing of any interlocutory matter at the primary stage of a case or in other words the case has yet not reached the stage of finality. In the final hearing of the case respective parties thereto would certainly be required to establish or prove their respective case completely or in other words conclusively. There would be total absence of alloy as regards establishment of the case either to have a relief sought from the court or for the rejection of the relief sought by the first party (Plaintiff) in the suit. The High Court Division was in serious error in allowing pre-emption only because prima facie it was established that Kulsuma and Rahima are sisters of Ilias Mia upon overlooking the material fact that establishing something prima facie is never the establishing of the said fact conclusively or finally or that said establishment i.e. prima facie establishment, was free from alloy. Making out of a prima facie case is nothing more than making out a case of first impression or something that appears to be true at the first sight or consideration. A prima facie case is not free from alloy or in other words it cannot be said that prima facie case has stood the acid test. As such establishing or making out of a prima facie case in law cannot be considered to have established the case finally or conclusively or said to have proved the case for having the relief sought by the first party in the proceeding conclusively or in other words free from alloy. 

 10. The High Court Division also was in error in placing reliance on the plaints of Title Suit No. 245 of 1979 and 344 of 1980 in arriving at the finding as to Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah in that the plaintiffs of the said suits in the respective plaints have made clear averment denying the fact of Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah. Merely because Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi have been made proforma-defendants in the aforementioned Title Suits it cannot be said the plaintiffs of the title suits accepted the said two defendants as the sisters of Ilias Miah as because there are statements in the plaints denying their being the sisters of Bias Miah and that there is also explanation in the plaints why these two defendants have been made parties in the suit. The said two title Suits are still pending and in the absence of decision in the said two suits or final disposal of the said two suits it can be said that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah, nor can it be said because of impleading Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi (as defendants) describing them as sisters of Ilias Miah in Tittle Suits a 'prima facie' has been made out by the preemptors as to Kulsuma Bibi's and Rahima Bibi's being the sisters of Ilias Miah. Since the pre-emptors did not establish by legal evidence that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah and that being so it cannot be said in the absence of legally establishing that Kulsuma Bibi and Rahima Bibi are the sisters of Ilias Miah, the pre-emptors by purchase from the said two persons have become co-sharers in the land left by Ilias Miah and that inherited by Ful Banu wife of Ilias Miah and that have acquired right of pre-emption.
